statement: Every positive involution of the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group acts by minus the identity on homology over Zp at every prime. Every primary homology map A_p is consequently faithful on every finite subgroup. The finite abstract subgroup types are exactly the nine realized types 1, C2, C3, C4, V4, C6, S3, D8 and D12. Dic12 is excluded by the exact three-adic normalizer obstruction, while D54 already excludes C12 and D24. Every order-four element has square minus the identity at all primes; a negative multiplier coordinate can only be an odd prime congruent to one modulo four, with the exact scalar matrix plus or minus a square root of minus one.
depends_on: D43 global involution multipliers; D46 actual positive involution homology and full fixed-group mod-two cohomology; the prime-independent closed-subgroup cusp argument of D48; D54 exact cover norm comparison; D33 finite order bound; D52 exact three-adic field normalizer and nine explicit realizations
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. D46's positive-involution conclusion is used for every positive involution, independently of whether it is a square. The global multiplier one is used in the exact peripheral equation 2z=-kappa. The odd-degree covering comparison is the actual deck-average splitting over Z2.
notes: The full cusp normalizer cannot contain an involution because D46 fixed groups have H1(-,F2)=0 and the finite-cover boundary character excludes a full cusp Z2 in such a subgroup. Its square exponent is therefore a two-adic unit. An invariant odd-prime cyclic character produces a type-(1,q) cover whose base homology has action minus identity and whose fixed boundary augmentation has action identity. The square norm vanishes modulo two, contradicting the primitive boundary power. This forces the full minus-identity matrix at every prime. For each finite subgroup, any nontrivial primary kernel would contain an involution or an order-three element; D43, D54 and the new positive-involution conclusion exclude all such elements. Faithful three-adic representation then excludes Dic12. The cyclic cubic and quartic scalar multiplier cases and geometric conjugacy remain explicit outstanding obligations; the nine-type result is a complete abstract existence classification.
